title: AP Top 25 predictions: Who will rise, fall and enter the new men’s college basketball rankings?
content:
Note: This story will be updated after the release of the AP Top 25 at 1 p.m. ET on Monday.

Five Top 25 teams lost in the second week of the college basketball season, from Duke and Kentucky going down in Tuesday’s Champions Classic in Chicago to Louisville falling on Sunday afternoon in Memphis.

How much will that shake up the poll? Let’s take a look at who’s likely to rise and fall.

It was a bad week if you’re a fan of one of the two major programs in Kentucky.

No. 24 Kentucky is likely to drop out of the Top 25 after losing by 20 to Kansas in the Champions Classic on Tuesday, then narrowly defeating Northern Arizona — picked to finish last in the Big Sky — at home Friday. Mark Pope’s Wildcats might be 3-1, but it hasn’t been convincing, particularly on defense. The Wildcats do get a chance to show some progress this Friday when they play Indiana on a neutral court in Indianapolis.

No. 10 Louisville will likely plummet, too. The Cardinals looked good for a half at Memphis on Sunday, then were outscored by 31 points in the second half of a 98-78 loss. Perhaps Memphis, which already beat Iowa State and VCU, is better than anticipated, but Louisville spent a lot of money building a roster via the transfer portal this offseason. It didn’t do that to give up 98 to Memphis.

Finally, we can expect No. 2 Duke and No. 3 Illinois to both fall out of the top five. Neither team suffered a “bad” loss — the Blue Devils fell by 6 to No. 5 Michigan State and the Illini also lost by 6, at No. 16 Texas Tech — but even one loss will have an impact this early in the season.

Let’s start with the Red Raiders. They’ve got plenty of room to climb from 16th after beating Illinois. If they crack the top 10, it will mark the third year in a row Texas Tech has spent at least one week there. One thing to keep an eye on if Texas Tech keeps winning: The Red Raiders have never been ranked in the top five.

Two teams just outside last week’s Top 25 that should pick up more votes: LSU and Memphis. We already mentioned Memphis’ wins above. But how about Will Wade’s LSU, which went to Spokane, Wash., and dug out an 81-80 win over No. 14 Gonzaga on Saturday? Whether or not LSU gets RJ Luis on the court — which is looking more possible than it did a week ago — the Tigers have made one of the season’s early statements. UCLA transfer Donovan Dent has three double-doubles in four games, and a 35-to-6 assist-to-turnover ratio.

Feast Week is still a week away, but college basketball’s early season tournament calendar begins Tuesday with the Players Era Eight — the first of two Players Era tournaments in Las Vegas this month. (Sixteen teams will play a bracket next week. Three ranked teams are in this set of eight: No. 1 Florida, No. 8 Houston and No. 15 Kansas.

There’s no guarantee the ranked teams will face each other, but if the favorites win, it would mean we get Florida-Houston in a semifinal on Wednesday (4:30 p.m. ET), and the winner could potentially play Kansas in the final on Thursday at 11 p.m. ET.
